verdicts.revised_claim: Bend 2 closures are affine. A record field of closure type cannot appear in a `Data` type, and applying the same closure twice (`f(f(s))`) is rejected. (Scope note: a closure CAN sit in a `Type`-kinded record and be called once, and a top-level def passed as a value is affine too. Only a `~` template function may be called repeatedly, and it must be closed and known at compile time.)

verdicts.revised_claim: Native code enters a Bend program only through foreign effect defs whose body imports `.c` and/or `.js` files. The `.c` file is spliced into the single emitted C file, and the `.js` file serves the JS lane. A foreign def must return base IO directly. Foreign code is entered only from the event loop's effect dispatch, never from pure or `!` code and never on the GPU. An effect can still push blocking work onto the runtime's IO helper threads via `io_work` (up to 64), and it can run arbitrary C or ObjC. So a native platform layer (windowing, input, OS text) has to be C or Objective-C. On the web lane it can be JS that calls exported pure Bend defs.

On the overstated part: guide/EFFECTS.md:60-63 says '`io_work(w, call, pack)` runs `call(w)` on a helper thread', and bend2/comp.ts:5612-5628 has io_work calling pthread_create(io_help) up to IO_HELP=64 (comp.ts:3468). bend2/effs/file_read.c and process_run.c use it. verdicts.revised_claim: Bend's only machine numbers are Nat, U32 and F32. There is no U64, I64, F64, I32, U16 or U8, and U32 has no signed ops (no signed compare, arithmetic shift or signed divide). Signed GPUI quantities such as i32 DevicePixels and isize tab_index must be two's-complement U32 with hand-written signed helpers, or F32. 64-bit entity ids and hashes must shrink: a Nat holds up to 2^48-1 on native (it fail-stops beyond that and does not wrap), so ids can be Nat or U32 pairs, while wrapping hashes have to be U32.

new_findings.finding: A GPUI-shaped core can be written in Bend 2 without @unsafe or mutual recursion. The sketch has a 20-kind Data element tree, a flexbox subset (row/column, padding, gap, flex-grow, justify start/center/end/between, align start/center/end/stretch, fixed/auto sizes, stacked overlay), a bottom-up measure pass, a top-down place pass, a hit list, defunctionalized Msg dispatch, an Array id-keyed entity store and a U32 trie. The trick is forest recursion: `case K{.., kids} <> t:` recursing on both `kids` and `t`, which the termination checker accepts. backplane-bend uses the same pattern (src/app/layout.bend:818-851) and has zero @unsafe across 221 .bend files and 11,822 defs. This supports P2's premise that framework logic can be pure Bend.
new_findings.evidence: research/v/bend-language/sketch/ui.bend (739 lines, 84 defs; @unsafe and `def f?(` appear only in comments). `bun bend/bend2/main.ts sketch/ui.bend --check-only` prints 'ALL PROOFS CHECK'. Running prints the layout tree: the Spacer with grow 1 takes 593.6px of free space, JBetween puts Progress at x=660, and JEnd right-aligns the last row at 780. Native output is identical to JS. measure is at 206, place at 339-347.

new_findings.finding: Bend's syntax rules carry a real tax. You cannot match on a computed value, cannot destructure a computed record (`Tot{..} = tot(..)` is refused), and a let cannot precede a match. Callees must be defined above callers. So the code needs many continuation shims: 14 of the sketch's 84 defs are `.k`/`.fin` helpers, plus several pick/selector helpers. Descending into a computed subtree (choosing lo/hi by a bit) needs a Nat fuel as the first argument. Constructor names share one namespace with Base, so GPUI-ish names such as `Scroll` collide with Base `Event.Scroll{}`, and Key, Mouse, Move, Close, Pix and Qua are also taken.
new_findings.evidence: Checker errors I hit: 'a parameter or field scrutinee (a match cannot scrutinize a computed value: give it its own def)' at `Tot{m, c, g, n} = tot(...)`; ''stack' can't be matched in this position (it is matched after a local statement ...)'; 'a fresh constructor name (duplicate declaration: Scroll)'; 'an unfilled law is a dead claim' when a callee was defined below its caller. The fixes are visible in sketch/ui.bend (flow_box.k, enter.k/enter.fin, kid_rect.fin, view.k1-k3, state.k1-k3, IMap.put/get with fuel).

new_findings.finding: The arity trap is 'an arity over 247', not 255. It hits only on native builds, and only when more than 247 words of unboxed scalar-record data are live across a non-tail call or a parallel let. Defs whose wide records are only passed through in tail position get inlined and do not trip it. A record that is recursive (boxed) avoids it. In a faithful port, a GPUI StyleRefinement (dozens of Option fields at about 2 words each) with two copies live across the recursive layout call would hit it, so style records should be boxed. Tree nodes are recursive and always boxed.
new_findings.evidence: bend2/comp.ts:136 (WIDE = 247) and 2821-2823 (die 'an arity over 247'); lay_of at 938-953 boxes non-recursive types over 247 words. Generated probes in exp/arity: c4x60 and p4x60 build and run. c4x62, c2x124 (live across a non-tail `cnt(n)`) and p4x62, p2x124 (live across `a b = cnt(n) cnt(n)`) give 'Error: an arity over 247'. The JS lane runs c4x62 (prints 2). c4x62_boxed.bend, which adds `up: Maybe<&2, R>`, builds and runs natively. Tail-passing variants (s3x120, s1x250) build, because sumr is inlined (no FID in the emitted C).

new_findings.finding: Affine closures do not fully rule out closure listeners. A closure can live in a `Type`-kinded tree and fire once (FnOnce-like). A fuel-bounded self-renewing handler `type Handler is Type: H{run: U32 -> Pair(U32, Handler)} | Spent{}` can be invoked repeatedly with no @unsafe. However, any closure makes the whole tree `Type`, so it can no longer be `+`-shared across the measure, place and hit passes the sketch relies on (`+kids` is used twice in place). Defunctionalized Msg stays the practical design, so the ranking does not change.
new_findings.evidence: exp/clo_renew.bend fires a renewing handler 3 times and prints 15 on JS and native (built with `-o out/clo_renew`). Without fuel, the checker rejects `counter(step)` inside the lambda with 'a decreasing self-call'. exp/clo_type_once.bend prints 42.

skeptics.summary: I re-checked the claims against a fresh Bend clone (565d7fd, the same as origin HEAD today) and by running code on both lanes. C1, C3 and C20 hold: closures are affine, defunctionalized Msg dispatch works, and there is no native library target. For C20, JS hosts do get a supported `.mjs` export. C7, C10, C16 and C17 are right in direction but overstated, so I revised them. Foreign C can run on the IO helper threads (`io_work`). A custom effect does not have to reuse `Window`, because a user affine `Type` wrapper over an id works on both lanes; it only loses unforgeability. Nat holds 48-bit ids. Base `Array<T>` already works as a U32-keyed entity store. To test expressibility I wrote a 739-line sketch with no @unsafe: a 20-kind element tree, flex layout, hit testing, Msg dispatch, an Array entity store and a U32 trie. It passes `--check-only` and gives identical output on the JS and native lanes. Mutual recursion is avoided with forest recursion, at the cost of many continuation shims. The arity trap is real but narrow: it appears natively when more than 247 words of unboxed records are live across a non-tail call or parallel let, and boxing the record fixes it. None of this changes the path ranking; if anything it backs P2's premise.

verdicts.revised_claim: Base `Event` (Key{code,down}, Mouse{x,y,button,down}, Move, Look, Scroll, Close) carries no typed text, IME, resize, focus or click-count, and Mouse has no modifier fields. On macOS a key code is the first UTF-16 unit of the lowercased charactersIgnoringModifiers, else 65536+keyCode. Modifier keys arrive as separate Key{65536+keyCode, down/up} events from flagsChanged, so an app can track modifier state itself. In practice a, Shift+a, Option+a and Cmd+a all give 97, while Shift+1 gives 33 ('!'), Up gives 63232 and Return gives 13. Shifted punctuation survives. Letter case can be rebuilt only from tracked Shift/Caps state. Option-composed characters and IME composition are lost entirely. Auto-repeat keyDowns are not marked as repeats.
verdicts.evidence: bend2/base.bend:78-84 is the Event type. window.c:70-73 maps keys (`[ev.charactersIgnoringModifiers lowercaseString]`, then characterAtIndex:0 or 65536+keyCode). :84-89 is flagsChanged, which pushes Key{65536+keyCode, (now&~flags)!=0}. :96-99 pushes Mouse with buttonNumber/down only, and isARepeat is never read. My probe (v/bend-window-runtime/keys/probe.c) builds real layout-translated NSEvents via CGEventCreateKeyboardEvent and `[NSEvent eventWithCGEvent:]`, then feeds them to BendView. It printed `Key{97 down} Key{97 down} Key{33 down} Key{97 down} Key{97 down} Key{63232 down} Key{13 down} Key{65592 down} Key{65592 up} Mouse{10,10 b0 down}` for a, Shift+a, Shift+1, Option+a ('å'), Cmd+a, Up, Return, shift press/release, and a shift+double-click (clickCount 2). verdicts.revised_claim: On macOS, an emitted program whose C contains a line starting with `#import ` (or any program with bangs) is compiled as Objective-C with `-fobjc-arc -fmodules`. Clang module autolinking then links AppKit, CoreText, Metal and the like with no user flags. CoreText text measurement from a Bend effect works.
verdicts.evidence: The decision is at bend2/main.ts:429-430, not 428-429 (428 is `const cc = cc_find(bangs)`): `const objc = mac && (bangs || /^#import /m.test(c)) ? ["-x","objective-c","-fobjc-arc","-fmodules"] : []`. The regex runs over the whole emitted C, so Base's window.c `#import`, which sits inside `#ifdef __OBJC__`, also triggers it. I rebuilt the CoreText effect against HEAD (v/bend-window-runtime/ct): it printed `CoreText width x1000: 143179`, and `otool -L ct/bin` lists /System/Library/Frameworks/CoreText.framework, CoreFoundation, Foundation and libobjc.

verdicts.revised_claim: `bend -o` has no CLI flag for extra libraries. The link line is objc flags + `-std=c11 -O3 file -lpthread -lm`, plus -lX11/-lasound on Linux when those headers appear, and GPU builds add -DBEND_METAL=1 or the CUDA flags. In-source link directives still work with stock clang, so linking a static library needs no CC wrapper, dlopen or hand-run clang. Option 1: put `__asm__(".linker_option \"-lNAME\"")` in the effect .c and set LIBRARY_PATH=<dir> at build time. Option 2: `#import` a header whose module map says `link "NAME"`, again with LIBRARY_PATH. SDK libraries whose module maps declare a link (zlib, sqlite3, ffi, ...) autolink from a bare `#import`, and the module import also sidesteps the FAR macro clash. `#pragma comment(lib)` does nothing on Mach-O, and `.linker_option "-L..."` is rejected. $CC is honored too, so a wrapper remains an option.
verdicts.evidence: main.ts:433-437 is the cpu/gpu arg lists, :398 is `ccs = [$CC, clang, clang-NN...]`, and :431-432 adds X11/asound only when `!mac`. Experiments in v/bend-window-runtime, all with stock Apple clang and no wrapper. (a) zmod: `#import <zlib.h>` with no push_macro and no pragma built and printed `zlib 1.2.12`; otool shows /usr/lib/libz.1.dylib (SDK zlib.modulemap has `link "z"`). (b) zinc: the same code via `#include` in a plain-C program fails with `Undefined symbols: _zlibVersion`. This is why the prior exp/lib failed: no #import, so no -fmodules. (c) zasm: `__asm__(".linker_option \"-lz\"")` in plain-C mode printed `zlib 1.2.12`. (d) dasm: a custom libdemo.a (a stand-in for a Rust staticlib) with `.linker_option "-ldemo"` fails without LIBRARY_PATH, but with `LIBRARY_PATH=$W/demolib bun bend/bend2/main.ts dasm/main.bend -o dasm/bin` it printed `demo 41`. (e) dmod: `#import "/abs/demolib/demo.h"` plus module.modulemap `link "demo"` and LIBRARY_PATH printed `demo 41`. (f) dL: `.linker_option "-L<dir>"` with no LIBRARY_PATH still gives undefined symbols. I did not test zui's own staticlib, whose transitive frameworks would need extra `.linker_option "-framework","X"` lines.

verdicts.revised_claim: Bend's effect C API (CID, io_eff, term_*/io_* helpers, Env internals) carries no ABI promise, and an open PR would break it right now: #1281 changes `io_eff(cid, run, need)` to `io_eff(cid, run)` and makes a third argument a compile error.

Rebuild your effects with every update." EFFECTS.md:3-5 notes that the guide is AI-written and pending human revision. verdicts.revised_claim: Window.frame is registered with need 0, so io_step runs it inline (io_exec) and keeps looping through the program's continuation without returning to io_loop. A render loop that never parks therefore starves timers, channels and spawned computations until it exits or parks. Adding IO.sleep(0) per frame (an IO_TIME park) fixes it.
verdicts.evidence: window.c:708 is `io_eff(CID(Window.frame), window_frame_run, 0)`. In comp.ts:5834-5870 (io_step), `need = io_eff_rows[c].ask`: a nonzero need goes to io_wait_on and returns, while need 0 runs `Term x = io_exec(e, a)` at 5863-5867 and loops. io_loop's timer and fd checks (comp.ts ~5900-5912) run only between io_step calls. sleep.c registers IO_TIME and spawn.c registers 0. I rebuilt both experiments against HEAD (v/bend-window-runtime/conc, conc2) and compared only output order, with numbers masked. conc printed `frames done`, then all 10 `tick gap` lines, then `ticker done`. conc2 (IO.sleep(0) in tick) printed all 10 ticks and `ticker done` before `frames done`. Under open PR #1281, Window.frame stays inline, and IO.sleep parks via io_wait_on with a deadline, so both the starvation and the workaround survive.

verdicts.revised_claim: Every App.run program contains a bang, because App.turn drops the previous frame with `Image.drop!(image)`. On macOS (and on Linux only when CUDA's nvrtc.h is present), `bend -o` therefore needs clang 19 / Apple clang 17 and runs `<bin> --gpu-build` to write `<bin>.gpu`. The .gpu is a cache, not a hard requirement: when it is missing, the binary prints a note and compiles the embedded Metal source at launch. On Linux without CUDA, an App.run program builds with clang 14, gets no .gpu, and runs the bang on the CPU cores. A program that drives Window.open/Window.frame directly, without App.run, has BANGS 0 and needs neither.
verdicts.evidence: base.bend:2947 is the App.turn def and :2954 is `Unit <- IO.pure(Unit, Image.drop!(image))`. main.ts:386-411 is cc_find (need = gpu ? (Apple ? 17 : 19) : 14). main.ts:426-427: `bangs = !/^#define BANGS\s+0$/m.test(c) && (mac || fs.existsSync(cuda + "/include/nvrtc.h"))`, and :438-439 adds the --gpu-build step. In comp.ts:4911-4934, gpu_load falls back to gpu_note plus a pipeline compiled from source when the archive is missing. Runs in v/bend-window-runtime: app/out.c (minimal App.run) has `#define BANGS   1`, while noapp/out.c (direct Window.open+frame) has `#define BANGS   0`. Building app produced bin plus bin.gpu, and noapp produced only bin. After `mv app/bin.gpu app/bin.gpu.bak`, `./app/bin` printed `bend: compiling the GPU program (.../app/bin.gpu is missing or stale)` and exited 0.

new_findings.finding: A user effect can extend Base's own BendView with an Objective-C category, because it shares the translation unit and is spliced after window.c. The category can adopt NSTextInputClient, route keyDown through interpretKeyEvents, and collect committed text into a side buffer that a second effect reads. Real typed text then arrives while Base's Window.open and Window.frame stay in use. P2's platform shim could therefore be a category plus a text-read effect instead of a replacement window. It binds to internal names (BendView, -key:down:), which carry no ABI promise per C11. In my non-frontmost run the input context had to be activated by hand.
new_findings.evidence: In v/bend-window-runtime/cat/text.c, `@interface BendView (Text) <NSTextInputClient>` overrides keyDown and implements insertText:replacementRange: into an NSMutableString. Text.take returns that buffer. Feeding layout-translated h,e,l,l,o (Shift on the first) printed `key 0 active 0 ctx 0x... conforms 1` and then `typed text: Hello`. Without `[v.inputContext activate]` the result was empty, because the window was not key in this terminal-launched run.

new_findings.finding: On HEAD, a program that reaches Window.open (and close) but never Window.frame does not compile on macOS: BendView references CID(Key), CID(Mouse) and CID(Look), which are emitted only when Window.frame is reachable. A P2 shim that replaces Window.frame with its own present effect must keep Window.frame reachable, or otherwise reference those Event constructors.

verdicts.revised_claim: GPUI's click API stores shared, multi-call closures: `on_click(listener: impl Fn(&ClickEvent,&mut Window,&mut App) + 'static)` pushes `Rc::new(move |..| listener(..))` onto `click_listeners`.
verdicts.evidence: zui HEAD 667d0aa, which matches origin after `git fetch`. crates/gpui/src/elements/div.rs:575-582 is `Interactivity::on_click`, which does `self.click_listeners.push(Rc::new(move |event, window, cx| listener(event, window, cx)))`. The fluent `StatefulInteractiveElement::on_click` at div.rs:1487-1493 delegates to it. div.rs:1596 defines `type ClickListener = Rc<dyn Fn(&ClickEvent, &mut Window, &mut App) + 'static>`. At div.rs:2825 the vector is cloned into a separate keyboard-activation handler (`let click_listeners = click_listeners.clone()`), and listeners are called in loops at 2852 and 2900. So one listener runs from several dispatch closures and on every event, which is a real shared multi-call closure. The other mouse listeners (div.rs:1579-1593) are `Box<dyn Fn>`: they are multi-call but not shared.

verdicts.revised_claim: zui's MacPlatform::run always blocks. Normally it calls NSApplication `app.run()`. In headless mode it calls `on_finish_launching()` and then `CFRunLoopRun()`, which also blocks. `Application::run_embedded` just calls `platform.run` and then returns a handle, so on macOS it blocks too. In zui only gpui_web (and the test platforms) implement a run that returns at once. zui contains no `pump_events` or `new_embedded`. gpuix gets both from its remorses/zed fork (`gpuix` branch). Because zui keeps MacWindow and the rest of gpui_macos `pub(crate)`, a non-blocking macOS host needs a patched gpui_macos, not just a custom `Platform` impl.

new_findings.finding: Provenance model of zui, for the user to mirror. zui is a one-shot verbatim source extraction, not a git fork and not a rewrite. A single squashed commit, 0b18592 (2026-08-25, by wingleeio, co-authored by Claude Fable 5), adds 385 files and 172,559 lines from wingleeio/zed at e2ddcc68. That is upstream zed-industries/zed f14fea9 (2026-07-19) plus comet patches. Zed's crate paths are preserved so that upstream fixes can be ported with `git -C ../zed format-patch -1 <sha> --stdout | git apply --3way`. The README nonetheless calls it "Zeron's fork of GPUI", and the GitHub description is "Zeron's standalone fork of GPUI" (fork:false, no parent). It keeps Apache-2.0, plus GPL-3.0 for the path crate, and a NOTICE crediting egoist/zed. None of the 47 commits since extraction port a Zed upstream commit; all are Zeron or contributor work (blur, edge fades, Windows/Linux fixes; 6 authors, PRs #1-#14). comet consumes zui pinned by git rev 667d0aa. This mechanism does not carry over to Bend. 'Standalone, not a fork' only works for zui because it is the same Rust source, so upstream diffs apply mechanically. A Bend codebase cannot take GPUI patches, so a Bend 'zui' would be a reimplementation that follows GPUI's design and API by hand. If code is translated it must keep Apache-2.0 attribution, and it is better described as GPUI-inspired than as a fork (bend-ui's research reached the same conclusion).

C22 holds: gpuix calls itself bindings, its native crate is a 26,125-line napi cdylib (it also builds for wasm) over the remorses/zed `gpuix` fork, and it uses that fork's new_embedded/pump_events. verdicts.revised_claim: Native code enters a Bend program only as `.c`/`.js` foreign effect files spliced into the single emitted C file. A foreign def must return base IO directly, and foreign code runs only on the event loop, never on the GPU. So any platform layer (windowing, input, OS text) has to be C or Objective-C, not Bend.
verdicts.evidence: comp.ts:2722-2735 (effect_srcs); bend.ts:3863-3872 ('a foreign definition returning base IO(...) directly'); GUIDE.md:408 ('Only the event loop runs them'). Nuance from my runs: the NSTextInputClient glue has to be Objective-C (v/ime-event-loop/ime.c, reentry/cbx.c), but the answers to its synchronous queries can be computed by Bend through the unsupported corpus_eval re-entry (reentry-state/run.txt). So the glue is ObjC, while the decision logic can stay in Bend.

verdicts.revised_claim: User-defined handle types are a WONTFIX design decision (#825), so a custom window or renderer effect has to reuse Base's linear `Window` handle. Doing so works: a custom effect can read the NSWindow/CAMetalLayer behind it.
verdicts.evidence: WONTFIX.txt:74 ('A handle type is a law of Base (#825)'). Extended in v/ime-event-loop: `Ime.attach(w: Window) -> IO(Window)` takes `io_hand_v(f[0])` as the NSWindow, adds a full-size NSTextInputClient subview and makes it first responder (log: 'attached: firstResponder=BimeView ok=1 inputContext=yes'). The stock Window.frame then pumps the subview's keyDown/interpretKeyEvents. One gotcha: Base's BendView returns acceptsFirstResponder YES (window.c:54-56), so it would take focus back on a click. The overlay therefore covers the view and forwards mouse events to it.

new_findings.finding: A per-frame snapshot design gives correct typed text and marked-text composition on macOS today, using only the normal effect API over Base's Window handle. Bend pushes {text, caret, marked length}. An ObjC NSTextInputClient overlay answers queries from a local copy and edits that copy optimistically, so later queries in the same pump see the edit. It queues insert/mark/unmark/command events, Bend drains them after Window.frame, applies them, and pushes the next snapshot. Uppercase, shifted and layout-specific characters arrived in Bend correctly, and so did real dead-key composition through Apple's TSM. All 14 snapshots matched the shim's prediction. The draft lists this as a P2 blocker ('IME needs synchronous OS-to-app queries'); it is not one.

new_findings.finding: The corpus_eval re-entry hack holds up beyond the trivial case at commit 565d7fd. Bend closures were applied synchronously from inside AppKit's TSM call stack while Base's Window.frame was pumping events. This worked with a capturing closure, a closure doing 65,535 parallel forks, and a closure containing a bang: 301 GPU dispatches, counted by a patched cube_run. It also survived 20,000 repeated calls in one callback, made possible by cloning capture-less closure nodes. With Bend-owned editor state threaded through C, selectedRange was answered by Bend right after insertText in the same pump. Results were correct in default GPU mode, with --gpu off and with --threads 1. The 'thread pool busy' worry does not apply by construction, because io_step runs an effect only after corpus_eval has returned with root_done. So the draft's P4 line 'There are no host-to-Bend callbacks' is overstated: synchronous callbacks work, but only through internals with no ABI promise. Those internals are task_node, FID(Clo~apply), corpus_eval, CORPUS/ALC, heap_alloc/cls_fit/fid_arity/term_clo for cloning, and ctr_take/spare_free for Tuple results. Callbacks from non-main threads (audio render, CVDisplayLink) would race the evaluator and remain unsafe.

new_findings.finding: These are GPUI's synchronous app queries on macOS. The snapshot design can answer the NSTextInputClient queries. What it cannot answer from data is GPUI's key routing, which asks the app synchronously whether a binding handled the key before the key goes to the IME. Covering that needs either a pushed keymap, including pending multi-stroke state and the accepts_text_input/prefers_ime_for_printable_keys flags, or Flutter-style deferred redispatch at the cost of about one frame of text latency. My prototype used a static rule instead: skip the IME when Cmd or Ctrl is held. characterIndexForPoint and firstRect for arbitrary ranges also need pushed glyph positions; the prototype answered NotFound and the caret rect. winit's minimal-state macOS IME shows what breaks when the snapshot is too thin.

Edits: insertText 3115, setMarkedText 3133, unmarkText 3156, doCommandBySelector 3191 (sets do_command_handled from the event_callback result). Key routing in handle_key_event 2464-2603: marked_text_range at 2501, query_prefers_ime_for_printable_keys at 2530, a DispatchEventResult from run_callback that decides whether inputContext handleEvent runs, apple_press_and_hold_enabled at 2573, and performKeyEquivalent returning BOOL (161, 2388). windowShouldClose 2937 returns should_close_callback(). Every PlatformInputHandler method calls cx.update on live state (crates/gpui/src/platform.rs:1417-1612; trait at 1625-1777). Flutter's macOS embedder is a production snapshot design that keeps a full local TextInputModel (ref/flutter_FlutterTextInputPlugin.mm insertText 796, markedRange 974, attributedSubstring 987). Its setEditingState comment at 566-571 admits stale ranges from a separate thread and clamps them. Its keys go to the text input only after the async framework reply (ref/flutter_FlutterKeyboardManager.mm 245-272). winit 0.30.13 (~/.cargo/registry/.../winit-0.30.13/src/platform_impl/macos/view.rs:263-267) returns NSNotFound from selectedRange, and winit master still does. Open issues trace to this: #4666 (dictation text dropped), #3617 (selected/replacement ranges ignored), #3342 (Character Viewer). Bend avoids Flutter's cross-thread race, because Base never runs [NSApp run] and pumps Cocoa only inside Window.frame (window.c window_wait). Queries therefore only arrive while the latest snapshot is installed.

Case for the rewrite reading: zui's README calls itself 'Zeron's fork of GPUI ... extracted into a standalone workspace', its root commit has no parents, and the user explicitly says 'Not a git fork, the same way zui is not a git fork ... whose code is Bend' and 'GPU-accelerated, GPUI-style UI framework'. gpuix is cited for its role (GPUI for language X), zui for its shape (a source-level fork with no shared history). Pick: rewrite. The target is a Bend 'fork' of GPUI's architecture and module layout (app/entity, window, elements, scene, text_system, platform traits as effect defs), with provenance discipline, not a binding.

new_findings.finding: 'GPU-accelerated' is not satisfied by P2 as drafted. With CPU-pool rasterization only the present kernel (window.c:359-384) runs on the GPU; that is a software renderer with a GPU blit, which is what backplane-bend already is on X11. The path the draft demoted to 'optional' is the one that matches the premise: the GPUI Scene (flat list of bounded primitives) is binned on the host into 64-px cells and rasterized by Bend code launched with one `!` per frame, exactly SHADERS.md's recipe (1920x1200 at 120 FPS on an M4 for a 3D scene), with the CPU pool as the automatic fallback since `--gpu off` runs the same bang on the cores. Verified constraint: this cannot live inside App.run. App.step evaluates `view(state)` as a pure argument (base.bend:2966-2972), the host binning forks before the bang, and a bang after a host fork in the same evaluation runs on the CPU (my fork.bend: GPU_PASS=0 even at --threads 1); an IO seam restores it (seam.bend: GPU_PASS=1). So P2-GPU needs a Slash-Boss-style custom loop (demos/app_slash_boss_3d/main.bend:2829-2835: scene, `IO.now()`, bang) and must sink the old Image inside the next bang instead of paying App.turn's `Image.drop!`. Ranking by fit to 'fully Bend + GPU-accelerated': 1) P2-GPU (Bend framework + Bend `!` tile rasterizer, ObjC glue only for window/input/CoreText), 2) P3 (GPUI-fidelity visuals, less Bend, macOS-only), 3) P2-CPU as P2-GPU's fallback rather than a separate path, 4) P4/P5 as API-design spikes. Open risks specific to P2-GPU that the benchmark agent must settle on a quiet machine: the bimodal GPU frame time, glyph-atlas sharing (needs `@unsafe Array.fork` or per-tile glyph lists), backdrop blur across tile edges, and the per-bang floor at 120 Hz.

new_findings.finding: Kill-factor assessment. (1) Allocator degradation: #1007 is open, labeled 'later', one community repro (oxura: 61 ms → 1013 ms over 24 rounds; KEEP_WORDS experiments made it worse), no maintainer response; #1307 was opened 2026-10-04 against 2.0.35 with zero comments; backplane hit it in production (board parse 0.2 s → 1.6 s over six runs) and worked around it with child processes. Both repros involve String/U32.show temporaries or Array-wrapped lists, not per-frame Image churn, so whether a UI that rebuilds a 5-10 MB quadtree every frame degrades over hours is untested. This is the one item that could kill a long-lived desktop app and the benchmark agent must run a 10k-frame headless build+drop loop comparing the first and last thousand frames. (2) Build cost (measured, correctness-of-workflow): Slash Boss (4,982 Bend lines → 122k-line, 3.3 MB C) builds in ~12 s (emit 1.4 s, clang -O3 8.1 s, Metal archive 2.5 s). backplane's server program (~47k reachable Bend lines → 793,924-line, 24.9 MB C) takes 40 s and 8.6 GB peak RSS for bun's emit plus 66.6 s and 6.2 GB for a single-TU `clang -O3 -c` on this 36 GB M3 Pro; backplane's own script documents the larger app as 'one ~30 MB C file on one core (minutes, ~20 GB)' and a Bun emit that grew past 28 GB, which is why they wrote cc-split.py, and that splitter now fails ('the emitted C changed shape'). There are no incremental builds (README:242) and the JS lane cannot open a window, so every UI tweak at framework scale is a 1-3 minute native rebuild. Not a kill; a steady tax. (3) Base namespace churn: constructor names are global, so Base growth (`Scroll` in 2.0.32) broke a 91k-line user program within a week; any framework must pin a Bend version, which EFFECTS.md already demands for effects.

skeptics.summary: The factual claims held up well: 19 of 25 are confirmed from the cited files and reruns, with only line-number or path nits. The draft's conclusions are where it breaks. Its premise reading (rewrite, not binding) is right but it then recommends a P2 whose default rasterizer is the CPU pool, which makes the product a software renderer with a GPU blit and fails the user's 'GPU-accelerated' requirement; the Bend-on-GPU tile rasterizer it demoted to 'optional' is the path that matches both constraints, and my gpu_pass-counter test shows it needs a Slash-Boss-style custom loop with an IO seam because a bang after host binning inside App.run's pure view runs on the CPU. 'Fully Bend' is quantifiable: about 87% of the macOS framework by zui-equivalent lines under P2 (82% under P3), with roughly 10.5k lines of window, input, clipboard, CoreText and display-link glue in Objective-C. The 4-8 month estimate is uncalibrated: the only large Bend UI, backplane-bend, is a bespoke 17.7k-line UI (not a 91k-line toolkit) written in 8 days with agents, and it no longer checks under Bend 2.0.35, so the real risk is daily churn and language traps rather than volume. Build cost is a tax not a kill (a 47k-line program costs ~107 s and 8.6 GB peak per native build, with no incremental mode), while the open allocator slowdowns #1007/#1307 remain the one unmeasured potential killer for a long-lived app that rebuilds a frame tree every tick.

measure.limiter: Best variant for UI-shaped frames (CPU pool, culling inside the bang at 1920x1200, N<=256): a 2-second `sample` of a separate 400-frame run (v/measure/prof/cpu12.sample.txt, not in the table) puts the top of stack in `spin_0`, the compiled flat per-pixel loop (ui_blit.i.c:2338, the tile's quad+glyph shading called from blk) with 2,697 samples, against 1,478 in `__psynch_cvwait`, 1,329 in `__workq_kernreturn` and 588 in `swtch_pri` (pool threads idle or yielding), 276 in `term_drop`, 133 in `spin_18`. So the pool variant is compute-bound in per-pixel SDF/sprite shading, with roughly 45-55% of pool thread time idle during the single-threaded phases (scene build 0.1-1.2 ms, the present kernel's 0.8-1.5 ms wait, drop). For the GPU variant (bin-gpu) the host sits in `__psynch_cvwait` for 8,871 of ~12,700 samples (waitUntilCompleted), so its limiter is the kernel's own GPU time; the density sweep shows that time is set by lane occupancy, not pixels: GPU-side render 23.9 ms for 370K leaves (N=4) vs 5.3 ms for 1.24M leaves (N=4096) at 1920, and 70-89 ms for N<=64 vs 19-22 ms for N>=256 at 3024, while the CPU pool is monotone in work (3.1 -> 8.9 ms). The runtime explains the mechanism: "A grow pass ends when its group is full or nothing grew, so a spine of forks unrolls whole" (comp.ts:4474-4475), i.e. in a sparse tree a 128-lane group fills with coarse tasks and each lane then runs its whole subtree serially. Two further GPU-side factors from the bang log: commit-to-GPU-start lag stays small (median 71-96 us, max 1.6 ms), so the bimodal slow frames (+10-20 ms, 14-25% of frames in sustained loops) occur inside execution; and idle gaps slow the GPU (sdf paced 8 ms: GPU-side median 1.5-1.9 ms vs 0.45 ms sustained), consistent with clock/power ramp-down, with external GPU load (median 60%+) as the other, unremovable contributor.

measure.verdict_detail: At 1920x1200 with a UI-typical scene (64-256 bordered cards + 2,000 glyph sprites) the host-binned `!` variant and the CPU pool are a tie within run-to-run spread (6.8 vs 6.1-7.1 ms; 7.8 vs 7.5-8.3 ms end to end; both hold the 120 Hz cap on the real window). The GPU leads only when the frame is dense (1,024 cards: 8.6 vs 10.6 ms, a gap larger than the spread; 4,096 cards at 3024x1964: 34.8 vs 38.8). The CPU pool wins by 2-8x on sparse, mostly flat frames (4-16 cards: 4.8-8.1 vs 16-31 ms) and at 2x HiDPI below 4,096 cards (e.g. 64 cards: 11.6-13.6 vs 100.8 ms), because Bend's GPU scheduler slows down as the fork tree gets sparser (lane under-occupation) while the CPU pool scales with work. Culling inside the bang is never viable (46-132 ms). Both prior explorers were partly right: bend-capabilities' "2x GPU win" was a mixed-mode artifact (CPU-pool render + GPU Image.drop at 17-19 ms/frame vs 10-11 ms all-GPU or all-CPU), and gpu-render-path's "CPU pool beats `!` on flat frames" holds and is the dominant regime for UI. The `!` lane's extra costs are a 1.2 ms GPU drop per frame, a bimodal slow mode (14-25% of frames at +10-20 ms under this machine's external GPU load) and a 3-4x penalty after idle gaps, all of which an event-driven UI would feel. All GPU numbers were taken under 35-65% external GPU utilization that I could not remove, so they are upper bounds; the CPU-side numbers were taken at load average 4.5.

new_findings.finding: Bend's GPU scheduler gets slower as the fork tree gets sparser: for the same shading, GPU-side render time is inversely related to live leaves (1920: 23.9 ms for 370K leaves at N=4, 10.1 ms at N=16, 5.1-5.4 ms for N>=64; 3024: 70-89 ms for N<=64 vs 19-22 ms for N>=256), while the CPU pool scales with work (3.1 -> 8.9 ms). Flat-collapsed UI frames are therefore the GPU lane's worst case even with host binning. Mechanism per the runtime: a grow pass ends when its 128-lane group is full, so coarse tasks in a sparse frontier run their subtrees serially per lane.

gaps.gap: Nobody measured the per-frame cost of the framework core. Every timing so far starts from a synthetic, pre-built scene. ui_blit's 'scene build' (0.1-1.2 ms) generates quads; it is not view + flex layout + text wrapping + hit test + Scene emission over a real element tree. The 739-line sketch (v/bend-language/sketch/ui.bend) proves the core can be written and is correct on both lanes, but it was never timed. The CoreText shaping round trip was never timed either: cons-list String to UTF-16, then glyph ids, advances and positions, then back into Bend for each changed line.
gaps.why_it_matters: The verdict rests on 'framework logic can be pure Bend' and on '120 Hz holds'. The headline 7.5-8.3 ms (CPU pool) and 7.8 ms (bin-gpu) at 1920x1200 already fill 90-100% of the 8.3 ms budget before any layout runs. Bend has cons-list strings, no mutual recursion and many continuation shims. If layout plus text for a 2k-5k node tree costs several ms, 120 Hz needs GPUI-style view caching or retained layout, and that is a different and much harder framework design.

| elements (rows) | glyphs wrapped and emitted | view | layout (measure + wrap + place) | paint | hit | whole core, one expression: median (range of run medians) |

### Verdict

Yes, it is viable, but as a GPUI-inspired reimplementation, not a port or a fork. Bend 2 can express the framework core without `@unsafe`: the element tree, flex layout, text wrapping, hit testing, message dispatch and the entity store. That core measured 0.17 to 2.15 ms per frame for trees of 500 to 5,000 elements. The most credible path is **P3**. It has three parts:
- the Bend core;
- one Objective-C effect file for the window, input, IME, clipboard and CoreText;
- a small Metal render pipeline that draws the Bend-built Scene by reading it straight out of the Bend heap.

The P3 prototype draws a frame of 256 cards and 2,000 glyphs in 0.42-0.47 ms at 1920x1200 and in 0.62-0.71 ms at 3024x1964. In a real Retina window it held 120 Hz with no missed frames.

"Fully written in Bend" can honestly mean about 82% of the macOS framework, counted in zui-equivalent lines. The rest, about 15k zui-equivalent lines, is the platform layer plus pixel shading, in Objective-C and MSL. It cannot mean Bend only. Native code enters a Bend program only through `.c`/`.js` effect files, and having Bend shade the pixels too (87% Bend, path P2) costs 16-39x more per frame and drops to 60 Hz on a full Retina redraw. It also cannot be a "fork" in zui's sense: no GPUI patch applies to Bend source, so the project would follow GPUI's design by hand.

### Overview

**zui** (zeronsh/zui at 667d0aa) is a one-shot verbatim extraction of Zed's GPUI: 152,848 lines of Rust and 4,530 lines of shaders, in a single squashed commit with no shared git history. "Standalone, not a fork" works for zui only because it is the same Rust source with Zed's crate paths kept, so `git format-patch | git apply` still carries upstream fixes across. By zui-equivalent lines, the framework logic a Bend version would rewrite is about 67k lines (gpui/src minus its test harness, plus scheduler, sum_tree, refineable and the small utility crates). The macOS platform layer is another 14k lines: about 10.5k of glue, 3.3k of Metal renderer and atlas, and 1.4k of MSL.

**Bend 2** (bendlang/bend at 565d7fd, version 2.0.35, unchanged upstream as of today) compiles a program to one C file. Pure code runs on a CPU thread pool, and code marked `!` runs on the GPU as a single compute kernel. Native code is reachable only through foreign effect files run by the event loop. Base's window takes a pixel quadtree (`Image`) and returns a batch of events. The project is 17 days past 2.0.0 with 35 point releases, and its README says the compiler is "99% AI-written".

**The core tension.** GPUI's control is inverted: AppKit owns the loop and calls stored closures (`Rc<dyn Fn>` listeners, five platform trait objects, synchronous IME queries). Bend owns its loop, pulls events once per frame, and has affine closures, closed sum types and no traits. Every design choice below follows from that mismatch.

**Prior art.** Nobody has reimplemented GPUI in another language. gpuix (napi plus wasm-bindgen over a forked GPUI), gpui-moonbit (a Rust staticlib with a cbindgen header) and gpui-react (Bun FFI) all bind native GPUI. backplane-bend shows that a large Bend UI app is possible. It has 17.7k Bend lines of UI, written in 8 days by two authors with Claude co-authoring 132 of 229 commits. But it is an app, not a framework, it is X11 only, it renders on the CPU, and it no longer type-checks under Bend 2.0.35.

**Reading of the request.** gpuix means "GPUI for language X", and the user also says "whose code is Bend" and "not a git fork, the same way zui is not". So the target is a rewrite (P2/P3). The binding shape (P4/P5) exists and is cheap, but none of GPUI's code would be Bend.

**Test conditions.** All measurements are from an Apple M3 Pro under sustained external load: load average 3-12, and 35-65% GPU utilization from other processes. Treat GPU-lane numbers as upper bounds.

### Key Concepts

- **GPUI frame.** Elements are rebuilt every frame and go through three phases. `request_layout` uses taffy, with a boxed measure closure for text. `prepaint` registers hitboxes and dispatch-tree nodes. `paint` fills the `Scene` with primitives and registers listeners for the next frame. The `Scene` is per-kind `Vec`s of `#[repr(C)]` primitives, which `MetalRenderer::draw_frame` encodes as instanced draws. Durable state lives in `Entity<T>`, which is updated through a take-and-reinsert lease (`EntityMap::lease`/`end_lease`).
- **Affine closures.** A Bend closure can be called at most once (`guide/GUIDE.md:83-85`). A closure field makes a type `Type`, never `Data`. GPUI listeners are shared and called many times (`div.rs:575-582` pushes `Rc::new(...)`), so in Bend they become **defunctionalized `Msg` data**, interpreted by one `update(msg, store)`.
- **`Data` vs `Type`, and `+`.** `Data` values can be shared with `+`, at a refcount cost (an atomic per read on the GPU). `Type` values have exactly one owner. A tree containing any closure turns into `Type` and can no longer be shared across the measure, place and hit passes.
- **Effects.** A foreign def's body is `import "./x.c"` and/or `import "./x.js"`, and it must return base `IO`. Only the event loop runs effects. Effects that need nothing to wait on (need 0) run inline in `io_step` and loop without yielding, which starves timers until something parks.
- **`!` (bang).** Offloads a call to the GPU only when it is the root task of an IO-step evaluation. A bang that comes after a host fork in the same evaluation runs on the CPU. The bang mark belongs to the **def**, not the call site. Device code is one compute kernel, `bend_dev`, with no vertex/fragment pipeline, texture sampler or blend unit. Its speed depends on how many GPU lanes the fork tree keeps busy (lane occupancy).
- **Handle laws.** `Window`, `File`, `Socket` and `Audio` are opaque linear handles that only Base may define (WONTFIX #825). A custom effect reuses `Window` and reaches the `NSWindow`/`CAMetalLayer` through `io_hand_v`. Alternatively it wraps a C-side id in a user `Type` record, which stays affine but can be forged.
- **In-place Scene read (P3).** The C effect walks the Bend Scene lists once and records only each node's heap word offset, 4 bytes per primitive. The shaders then read every field directly from the Bend heap, which is wrapped as a no-copy `MTLBuffer`.
- **IME snapshot.** Each frame, Bend pushes `{text, caret, marked range}` to an Objective-C `NSTextInputClient` view. That view answers AppKit's synchronous queries from its local copy, applies edits optimistically, and queues them for Bend to drain after the frame.
- **Damage tracking.** Keep the previous frame's `Image` quadtree and re-rasterize only the cells that touch a dirty rectangle. Bend-side rasterization needs this at Retina. P3 does not.

### How It Works

One frame of the recommended P3 design, from OS event to pixels:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  OS["AppKit: NSEvent, TSM/IME, vsync"] --> SH["ObjC shim: event queue + NSTextInputClient view"]
  SH -->|"Ev.drain effect: events as a Bend list"| DIS["Bend: hit list + focus path + keymap -> Msg list"]
  DIS --> UPD["Bend: update(msg, store) over Array slot table"]
  UPD --> VIEW["Bend: view(state) -> Element tree (closed sum, Data)"]
  VIEW --> TXT{"Bend: text runs missing from shape cache?"}
  TXT -->|"yes"| CT["ObjC: CoreText shape effect -> glyph ids, advances"]
  CT --> LAY
  TXT -->|"no"| LAY["Bend: measure, wrap, place (flex subset)"]
  LAY --> PAINT["Bend: paint -> Scene lists + hitboxes"]
  PAINT -.->|"push snapshot: text, caret, marked range, keymap"| SH
  PAINT -->|"P3.present effect: walk lists, 4 bytes per primitive"| ENC["ObjC: encode instanced draws, glyph atlas (CoreText raster on miss)"]
  ENC --> MSL["MSL: vertex/fragment shaders read Bend heap in place, blend hardware"]
  MSL --> PRES["CAMetalLayer present, vsync"]
  PRES --> SEAM["Bend: IO.sleep(0) seam so timers and channels run"]
  SEAM --> OS
```

1. **OS event (native).** AppKit delivers an `NSEvent`.
   - GPUI turns it into `PlatformInput` in `handle_view_event` (`gpui_macos/src/window.rs:2605`) and calls a stored closure right away.
   - Bend never calls `[NSApp run]`. Base pumps Cocoa only inside `Window.frame` (`effs/window.c:408-423`). In P3 the present effect pumps events itself, as `p3_go` does at `p3fx.c:267-272`.
   - The shim queues events. Typed text comes through `interpretKeyEvents` into an `NSTextInputClient` that Bend owns. Base's own key codes lose case, Option characters and IME (Shift+a and Cmd+a both arrive as 97).
   - Two ways to attach that view were verified: an overlay subview that becomes first responder, or an Objective-C category on Base's `BendView`.
2. **Drain (effect).** After presenting, Bend calls a drain effect that returns the queued events as a Bend list. This is GPUI's control flow reversed: GPUI is called by the OS, Bend polls once per frame.
3. **Dispatch (Bend).** Mouse events are hit-tested against last frame's hitbox list. Key events walk the focus path and the keymap, keeping multi-stroke pending state in Bend.
   - GPUI runs every paint-registered mouse closure for every event (`window.rs:5202-5258`). In Bend each hitbox carries a `Maybe<Msg>` instead.
   - Synchronous OS questions are answered from data pushed the frame before:
     - "Did a binding handle this key?" needs either a pushed keymap or a one-frame redispatch. GPUI asks this synchronously in `handle_key_event`, `gpui_macos/src/window.rs:2464-2603`.
     - `windowShouldClose` is answered the same way.
   - If pushed data is not enough, the `corpus_eval` re-entry hack can run Bend synchronously inside AppKit's callback stack. It survived 20,000 calls, forks and 301 GPU bangs, but it uses internals with no ABI promise.
4. **Update (Bend).** `update(msg, store)` rewrites the state.
   - Entities are U32 ids into a Base `Array<Ent>` used as a slot table, threaded linearly through `view`. Sparse keys use a roughly 60-line U32 trie.
   - There is no `Rc` and no `Drop`, so handles are not released automatically. Use explicit `release(id)` or a per-frame sweep from window roots.
   - GPUI's lease pattern maps directly, because Bend's ownership model already is take-then-reinsert.
   - Signed quantities such as `DevicePixels: i32` and `tab_index: isize` become F32 or two's-complement U32 with hand-written signed helpers. Bend has no U64 or F64, and Nat ids fail-stop above 2^48-1.
5. **View (Bend).** `view(state)` builds a closed-sum `Data` tree (`Div | Text | Img | List | UniformList | Button ...`).
   - There are no traits, so `AnyElement`, `dyn Action` and `TypeId` matching become constructor tags. A user-defined element means adding an arm, or using a `Custom{kind, data}` escape hatch.
   - There are no macros, so the roughly 114 Tailwind-style style methods are written by hand or generated as Bend source.
   - Recursion over the tree is "forest recursion" (`case K{.., kids} <> t:`), because mutual recursion needs `@unsafe`.
6. **Text (effect, then Bend).** GPUI calls CoreText synchronously from taffy's measure closure. Bend cannot, because shaping is IO and layout is pure. So the frame is staged:
   - collect the text runs missing from the shape cache;
   - shape them in one CoreText effect;
   - then lay out purely.

   The measured round trip is 0.36 ms for a 2,000-character block, or about 10 µs per changed 80-character line. Strings are cons lists of characters, so the shape cache is keyed per line.
7. **Layout (Bend).** A bottom-up measure pass, a greedy word wrap over cached advances, then a top-down place pass. The prototype covers row/column, padding, gap, flex-grow, justify, align and stretch. GPUI's `Style` also has grid and block layout (`style.rs:170-328`, `770`), so "a flex subset replacing taffy" understates the eventual layout engine.
8. **Paint (Bend).** Emit a flat Scene (quad list plus glyph-sprite list), the hitbox list and the IME snapshot.
   - The whole core (view, layout, paint and hit test) costs 0.171 / 0.803 / 2.15 ms for 501 / 2,001 / 5,001 elements.
   - It runs on one core. List recursion does not parallelize, and 1 thread and 12 threads give the same time.
   - It must stay off the `!` lane: `layout!` took 14.4 ms at 501 elements and crashed with a machine stack overflow at 2,001.
9. **Present (native).** `P3.present(win, qs, gs)` walks the two lists, which takes 8-12 µs and records 4 bytes per primitive, and encodes two instanced draws. The fragment shaders compute the rounded-rect SDF and border from fields read in place, and blend premultiplied-over in hardware.
   - The effect takes the lists as `IO(Window & Qs & Gs)` and hands them back. Bend's affine typing therefore keeps the Scene alive while the GPU reads it.
   - A production version would keep the glyph atlas texture on the C side (CoreText rasterizes on a miss, as GPUI's `paint_glyph` does) and put tile ids in the Scene. Keeping texels in a shared Bend tree cost 4x at 2x resolution, because of refcount traffic.
10. **Yield (Bend).** End each frame with `IO.sleep(0)`. Present effects run inline with need 0, so a loop that never parks starves timers and channels for the whole run.
    - Skip `App.run`. It adds an `Image.drop!` bang every frame (`base.bend:2954`).
    - Without it, the binary has `BANGS 0`: it builds with clang 14+, ships no `.gpu` archive, and avoids the mixed-mode tax (17-19 ms vs 10-11 ms per frame) and the per-def bang trap.

**Recommendation: P3.**
- **Speed.** It is the only path measured to hold 120 Hz at 2x with full redraws. On the same 256-card scene it is about 16-20x faster than the best P2 variant at 1x and 23-39x faster at 2x. That removes the need for damage tracking, which is the hardest piece of P2.
- **Visuals.** Alpha, hardware blending and antialiased SDF edges come for free. Blur and MSAA paths can be ported from zui's `metal_renderer.rs` and `shaders.metal`, which a quadtree `Image` cannot express.
- **No `!`.** It needs no bang anywhere, which sidesteps all of the measured `!` traps.
- **Cost.** It is probably not more work than P2. The renderer prototype is 349 lines of C including the MSL, while P2 needs a Bend rasterizer, a glyph atlas in Bend and a damage-tracking image design.
- **Honesty.** The pixels are shaded by MSL, not Bend.
- **Keep the Bend rasterizer as a fallback.** Use P2-CPU with damage tracking where Metal is absent, for example Linux on X11 following backplane's effect. Windows is not a Bend host at all (WONTFIX #788).

Bend can rasterize on the GPU. Slash Boss reproduced its documented speed here: 7.2-8.3 ms per frame, 3 runs of 1,192 frames, against SHADERS.md's 8.0 ms on an M4 mini. It loses for UI for three reasons:
- UI frames are mostly flat, and flat frames leave GPU lanes idle. At 4 cards the GPU-side render takes 23.9 ms, against 5.3 ms at 4,096 cards.
- 2x resolution multiplies that cost.
- The framework core cannot run on `!` at all.

### Risks and gotchas

**What could kill the project**
1. **Upstream churn plus no ABI promise.** This is the most likely killer.
   - The effect C API is internal by design. Open PR #1281 changes `io_eff(cid, run, need)` to `io_eff(cid, run)`, which would break every effect.
   - Base constructor names are global. Base's 2.0.32 `Scroll` broke backplane's 91k-line program within a week.
   - P3's shaders hard-code Bend's node layout: field offsets, the refcount redirect (`term_rfc`, `LOC_MASK`), and F32 stored in the low word.
   - Mitigations: pin a Bend commit; run a startup self-test that renders a known Scene and checksums it (the `P3_CHECK` path already dumps the texture); or copy fields into a packed buffer during the walk. The copy is estimated at tens of µs, not measured.
2. **Allocator degradation (#1007, #1307).** #1007 reproduces at HEAD: 2.7x slower on 1 thread and 18x on 12 threads. But it is a working-set effect: +25% at 160K characters per round, 3.7x at 329K. A UI rebuilding about 2,000 characters and 200 String keys per frame showed no slowdown over 20,000 frames. A text-heavy app (an editor buffer) must cache text per line. Runs longer than 20,000 frames were not tested.
3. **Text editing depth.** Typed text, dead keys and marked text through the snapshot design matched 14 of 14 snapshots. But that used synthetic keystrokes on the German layout only: no real Japanese or Chinese IME was exercised, and candidate-window placement and reconversion are untested. `characterIndexForPoint` and per-range rects need pushed glyph positions.
4. **Build loop.** There are no incremental builds and the JS lane cannot open a window. A small UI program builds in about 3.3 s and Slash Boss in 12.1 s. A 47k-line program took 107 s and 8.6 GB peak memory. At framework scale, every tweak becomes a 1-3 minute native rebuild.
5. **Reach.** P3's renderer is macOS only. Linux needs P2-CPU with an X11 shim. Windows is not supported (#788).

**Gotchas**
- **The bang flag is per def.** If any call site uses `f!(...)`, a plain `f(...)` in the same binary also went to the GPU: 16.6 ms, and a stack overflow at 2,001 elements (`comp.ts:1376-1377`, `2836`, `5260`). Keep `!` out of framework code.
- **`App.run`.** Every frame it runs an `Image.drop!` bang. Rendering on the CPU pool with the GPU lane on cost 17-19 ms vs 10-11 ms per frame. Write your own loop instead.
- **Starvation.** `Window.frame` and any need-0 present effect starve timers until something parks. End every frame with `IO.sleep(0)`.
- **Base window without `Window.frame`.** A program that opens Base's window but never reaches `Window.frame` fails to compile on macOS: `BendView` references `CID_KEY`, `CID_MOUSE` and `CID_LOOK`. The P3 prototype also drops Base's event batch, so the shim needs its own drain effect.
- **Arity trap.** More than 247 words of unboxed records live across a non-tail call is a native build error. Box style records, such as a GPUI `StyleRefinement`.
- **Linking.** Use `__asm__(".linker_option \"-lNAME\"")` plus `LIBRARY_PATH`, or a module map with `link`. A bare `#import` autolinks SDK libraries and avoids the runtime's `FAR` macro clash. `#pragma comment(lib)` does nothing on Mach-O.
- **AppKit details.**
  - Copy the string passed to `insertText:`; AppKit reuses it, and text arrived empty without the copy.
  - Base's `BendView` returns `acceptsFirstResponder YES`, so an overlay view must forward mouse events or it loses focus on a click.
- **Proof gate.** Any def that depends on foreign code fails `--check-only`, so laws must import only pure modules.
- **Syntax tax.** Bend cannot match on computed values, cannot destructure a computed record, and requires callees above callers. In the sketch, 14 of 84 defs are continuation shims.
- **Idle cost.** Base presents every vsync and an idle loop's CPU/GPU use was not measured. A blocking event wait has to be bounded by the next timer deadline.

**Upstream changes that would unblock**
- **PR #1108** (`open_resizable`, `Resize`, backing scale). It would remove the shim's resize and HiDPI work, but not text or IME. It is open, labeled `later`, 74 commits behind main, and no longer applies cleanly. It also silently doubles drawable and mouse coordinates for existing Retina programs.
- **#813, native library target.** It would make host-to-Bend calls supported, which would make GPUI-style synchronous IME and key-routing queries and the P4 callback design legitimate instead of the `corpus_eval` hack. The GitHub issue is closed as not planned. `WONTFIX.txt` lists it under SOON as "planned, not scheduled".
- **U64 (#1027) and F64 (#1120).** These would let entity ids, 64-bit hashes and f64 geometry map directly. F64 would not help on the GPU, because Metal has no f64. Both GitHub issues are closed, and both are listed in SOON as "we will add it ourselves; we do not merge PRs". Neither exists at HEAD.
- **#825, user handle types.** These would give unforgeable `Surface` and renderer handles. Upstream: "we will address the gap later".
- **#1019 and #1022** (typed text, IME in Base) would shrink the shim. Fixes to **#1007/#1307** would remove the per-line caching constraint.
